Workspace-backed state init, join, delete, and verify logic for txn, rec, and alloc data.

# Purpose
This C file implements the life cycle and integrity checks for `fd_funk`, a shared-memory data structure that stores transaction and record state. It provides functions to report the required alignment and memory footprint, create a new instance in shared memory with [`fd_funk_new`](<#fd_funk_new>), attach a local handle with [`fd_funk_join`](<#fd_funk_join>), detach with [`fd_funk_leave`](<#fd_funk_leave>), and destroy the shared object with [`fd_funk_delete`](<#fd_funk_delete>) or [`fd_funk_delete_fast`](<#fd_funk_delete_fast>). The code also sets up and tears down the internal parts of the object, including the transaction map and pool, the record map and pool, and the allocator used for value storage.

The file also defines [`fd_funk_verify`](<#fd_funk_verify>), which checks that the shared-memory object and its joined view are consistent. It validates the magic value, workspace addresses, transaction and record limits, map seeds, child indices, root transaction state, and allocator state. The code uses workspace address translation, scratch allocation, and explicit memory fences to manage shared-memory layout and object publication in a controlled way.
